issues.what: Brief planned-moment text pasted into prose (also ch2, ch5, ch8)
issues.quote: The train stops inside the tunnel and every lamp in first class goes out at once.

issues.what: Geography wrong going down: Dharampur is after Barog, yet the train passes it before the tunnel; ch2 repeats it
issues.quote: 21:40. Dharampur. 22:15. The tunnel approach.

issues.what: The unsent telegram is found again in the same breast pocket as if new, with different wording; a third copy appears in ch7
issues.quote: In the breast pocket, a folded paper. A telegram form. Unsent.

issues.what: Ch3 and ch4 share the title 'The Bolted Door'
issues.quote: Chapter 4: The Bolted Door

issues.what: Major's 'leave one question unasked' plea repeated as new in ch2, 3, 5, 6 and 8; ch5 claims it was made 'at Solan'
issues.quote: At Solan you said leave the wire till daylight.

issues.what: Vivienne boarded at Shimla on a booked name in ch1; ch4/5/8 say Summer Hill, cash fare, no reservation
issues.quote: You boarded at Summer Hill on a cash fare

issues.what: Vivienne's nails: bitten under polish (ch1), chipped varnish (ch2), unpainted (ch4), dark red (ch5)
issues.quote: Her nails were short and unpainted.

issues.what: Timetable, the promised key to the solution, contradicts itself: Up leaves Kalka 12:20 (ch4) vs Up 71 left Shimla 16:20 (ch6); stop at 21:47 vs 22:15-22:31
issues.quote: Up 71 left Shimla 16:20. Due Solan 18:41

issues.what: Dev is a Kalka taxi driver of 22 who saw Vivienne off (ch5), then a second-class leave boy from Solan (ch7), then 19 (ch8)
issues.quote: He is twenty two. He drives a taxi in Kalka

issues.what: Unfair solution: Rosalind 'heard' an 18:03 engine at Solan though she was in Shimla then; gloves multiply (Vivienne's brown pair, one in trunk, one on Tashi, one on crate); Lal dies of an unclued heart condition
issues.quote: At Solan, before the wire died. A B class exhaust

issues.what: Meta text addressing the reader
issues.quote: what she had covered with the rug in Chapter 1

issues.what: Real brand name
issues.quote: Bryant and May, half full

issues.what: 'Crown carriage' is wrong for Indian Railways in 1962
issues.quote: poured oil against a Crown carriage

praise: The opening chapter's snowbound tunnel, the four wicks screwed down, and Rosalind counting everything make a genuinely atmospheric closed-room setup.

issues.what: Year-digit maths wrong: a 2016 cut would wear a 6, and 2021 being five years ago makes this 2026, so ready trees were cut in 2017
issues.quote: painted last winter to mark nine years since 2016

issues.what: 1 and 6 are not neighbouring keys; typo should come from misreading the flat-topped handwritten 1 as a 7 (ch2, ch3, ch4 say 6)
issues.quote: A single digit slipped one key to the side.

issues.what: Factory says the thief 'left one behind' though the only thin plank is in Rosaria's kerchief from the ditch; ch4 then has a thin plank at the factory and bark at the tree's foot too
issues.quote: He left one behind when they measured.

issues.what: Chapter restarts at dawn and replays ch1/ch3 as new: Leitao re-accuses Joaquim, Rosaria re-explains the typo, Tiago repeats the lorry; ends with 'sixty planks' held
issues.quote: The yard was still blue when Rosaria took the south path.

issues.what: Joaquim's night walks: forty years in ch1, twenty in ch3
issues.quote: I have done it twenty years.

issues.what: One 'plank' per tree is a simplification (a tree yields several planks); left as the story's shorthand
issues.quote: Sixty planks gone meant a lorry

fix: Ch1: correct the year digit (7 = cut 2017) and the typo mechanism; ch2-ch3: 6 becomes 7, Joaquim's forty years; ch3: factory holds the man, not a thin plank; ch4: rewrite to continue the same afternoon from the phone call without replaying earlier scenes.
praise: The five-year tree is a lovely, fair clue shown plainly in chapter one, and the bark-and-hatchet detail feels lived-in.

issues.what: Mr Barasa plays the violin with the bow, then the bow is missing
issues.quote: He pulled the bow across the strings.

issues.what: Physically impossible: a full-length bow cannot be pushed through a violin's f-holes; Njeri also says she hid it high
issues.quote: Then the missing bow, with all its hairs covered in fluff.

issues.what: Six big footprints are never explained, so the 'one too many' count does not quite play fair
issues.quote: Six prints were big, size like her own boots.

issues.what: Child climbing on a bench to hide things is shown without a grown-up's word on safety
issues.quote: Then I stood on the bench to hide it high

issues.what: Notebook case name differs from the title; Wanjiru shakes a shaker, not the drum
issues.quote: THE CASE OF THE QUIET VIOLIN

fix: Ch1: pluck rather than bow at the start; stuff only a ribbon and hanky inside; put the bow on top of the cupboard next to the bench; explain the six big prints as Mr Barasa's; add a gentle safety line; tidy the notebook title and the drum line.
praise: Warm, funny and kind: Otieno's counting cracks the case and Wanjiru's 'I am sometimes wrong' lands without preaching.
